classification.difficultyReason: Link successive right triangles using each previous hypotenuse, then extend the demonstrated unit-leg construction to obtain √5.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the values of $x$, $y$ and $z$ in the diagram below.

spec.description: Three successive right triangles fan upwards from a common vertex. Four unit labels and three right-angle markers retained; decorative blue region fills omitted.
spec.mathematics: First hypotenuse x, next y, final z; each new perpendicular outer leg has length 1.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source variables and unit givens are visible; calculated lengths are withheld.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=1^2+1^2\\x&=\sqrt2\\y^2&=x^2+1^2\\y&=\sqrt3\\z^2&=y^2+1^2\\z&=\sqrt4=2\end{align*}$$
Only the positive roots represent lengths.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The above diagram gives a way of constructing segments of length $\sqrt2$, $\sqrt3$ and $\sqrt4$. Show how you could extend the diagram to construct a segment of length $\sqrt5$.

answer.short: At the outer endpoint of the side of length $z$, draw a unit segment perpendicular to that side. Join its new endpoint to the common vertex; this gives a segment of length $\sqrt5$.
answer.worked:
Extend the fan by drawing a segment of length $1$ perpendicular to the side of length $z$ at its outer endpoint. Join the new endpoint to the common vertex. If the new hypotenuse is $w$,
$$\begin{align*}w^2&=z^2+1^2\\w^2&=4+1\\w&=\sqrt5\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete original fan plus one perpendicular unit segment and the requested new hypotenuse.
spec.mathematics: The new right triangle has legs 2 and 1, so its hypotenuse is sqrt(5).
spec.answerVisibility: The extension and sqrt(5) label appear only in answer editions.
